diffs.classMap: Not obfuscated, and it has the same class names as 1.8: Bounce=Bounce, Ball=Ball, BounceCanvas=BounceCanvas, BounceUI=BounceUI, Local=Local, Profile=Profile (byte-identical class file), TileCanvas=TileCanvas, TileCanvas$GameTimer=TileCanvas$GameTimer. There is no BounceConst class. Its constants are declared where they are used: physics and scoring in Ball (Ball.java:40-84), tile and image IDs, colours and sizes in TileCanvas (TileCanvas.java:44-236), HUD layout in BounceCanvas (BounceCanvas.java:46-64). Field renames only: Ball.myParent is 1.8 Ball.mCanvas, and BounceCanvas.myBall is 1.8 BounceCanvas.mBall. Ball has an extra unused field mCDEdgeFlag. Both class sets carry LineNumberTables. All line numbers below are CFR lines in <ver>/cfr/com/nokia/mid/appl/boun/<File>.java.

differences.what: Game timer period

No speed clamp. 1.8 clamps ySpeed and xSpeed to [-150,150] at the start of each update, before the vertical loop. 1.01 has no clamp, so stacked rubber jumps (jumpOffset -10 per rubber bounce with UP held), jump bonus and ramp redirects can give |speed|>150, which means more pixels per step.
differences.thisVersion: Ball.java:716-721: nothing between the slideCntr update and the vertical loop

differences.what: A floor bounce does not end the vertical movement loop. In 1.8, once the ball hits the floor (or the ceiling under reversed gravity), ySpeed=-ySpeed/2, grounded=true, and the loop is left with break (bytecode goto 946, outside the loop). In 1.01 the loop keeps running (goto 854 = i++), and its bound abs(ySpeed)/10 is re-read with the new halved, reversed speed. If i+1 < |new ySpeed|/10, the ball moves back up the remaining pixels in the same step. Each such move sets mGroundedFlag=false (Ball.java:728). That has two effects: (a) no jump on that landing, because the jump test at Ball.java:807 needs grounded, so the ball makes a natural half-speed bounce and jumps on a later, slower landing; (b) gravity is applied after the loop that step.
differences.baseline: Ball.java:814-830 (break after the bounce in every case)

differences.what: Ceiling rebound speed is ±6 instead of ±20. After hitting a ceiling (or the floor under reversed gravity), ySpeed = bl?-6:6. Because |6|/10=0, the rest of the vertical loop is skipped that step. In 1.8 it is ±20, which allows up to one more pixel that step and a faster drop.

When a large ball leaves water mid-loop, ySpeed is halved with integer division (rounds toward 0) instead of an arithmetic shift (rounds toward -inf). The two differ for odd negative ySpeed (for example -15 gives -7 in 1.01 and -8 in 1.8), and that feeds the following |ySpeed|<=10 → 0 snap.

No wall bounce. In the horizontal loop, when the ramp flag is set and both diagonal moves are blocked, 1.8 reverses and halves xSpeed (xSpeed = -(xSpeed>>1)). 1.01 has no else branch, so xSpeed is kept and the ball keeps pushing into the wall.

Plain (non-rubber) ramps 30-33 redirect the ball at full speed. In 1.01 the triangle redirect swaps speeds at full value for all 8 triangles (31,33,35,37: x=y,y=x; 30,32,34,36: x=-y,y=-x). In 1.8 only the rubber triangles 34-37 swap at full value; plain triangles 30-33 halve (x=y>>1,y=x>>1 or x=-(y>>1),y=-(x>>1)). triangleCollide and TRI_TILE_DATA are identical.

Wrong collision position when the ball centre is above the top of the buffer (y<0). For y<0, 1.01 sets k=|y|/12+1, y=0, firstRow=(0-half)/12-k=-k, lastRow exclusive=1, globalBallY=-half-12k (+tileY*12). The pixel mask is therefore tested with its centre snapped to -12k, i.e. -12 for y in [-1,-11] and -24 for y in [-12,-23], instead of the real position. 1.8 keeps the real globalBallY and only shifts the row range by 12 px (n3=12). Consequences when jumping through the top edge into the screen above: hits against row tileY-1 are tested at a different height; row tileY-2 is not tested until the centre reaches -12, so the ball can rise up to about 5 px further and end up overlapping a brick after the flip (+84). The same applies to the horizontal moves and ramp moves made while y<0.

No hoop rims (no edgeCollide). 1.8 has small rim rectangles (HOOP_EDGE_DOWN_BY 6, IN_BY 11) that make hoop edges solid. Active hoops in 1.8: on a rim hit, tile 23 is solid and gives no ring; tiles 15,24,16,21,13 are solid but still give the ring; 14 and 22 have no rim. Inactive (already collected) hoops in 1.8: 17,19,20 are solid at the rim for the small ball (solid when thin-hit for the large ball); 18 is solid only for the large ball; 25,27,28 are solid at the rim for any ball; 26 is passable. In 1.01, active hoops are pure triggers: 23,24,21,22 always collect; 13,14,15,16 collect for the small ball and are solid (thin rect) for the large ball. Inactive 17-20 are solid only for the large ball (thin rect). Inactive 25,26,27,28 are fully passable.
differences.thisVersion: Ball.java:433-439 (0,8,25,26,27,28 passable), 503-586 (hoop cases, no rim test), 579-586 (17-20: thinCollide && large → solid)

differences.what: Collecting a hoop clears the water flag of its two tiles. 1.01 writes plain 145-156 (dirty|17..28). 1.8 ORs in the tile's 0x40 water bit. Wet hoops exist in level 3 (74,33-34), level 5 (54-55,22), (48-49,25), (60-61,25), level 7 (43,12-13), level 8 (66,15-16), (110,15-16), (88,19-20), and level 11 (121-122,44), (165-166,49), (47-48,53), (110,54-55), (154,54-55). After the pass, those two tiles behave as air: air gravity and maximum speed, the large ball no longer floats there, and the water halving test (Ball.java:729) applies. They are also drawn with the sky colour instead of water. (Checkpoints 128/136 and extra life 128 lose the water bit in both versions.)

Closed exit is passable. In 1.01, tile 9 does something only if thinCollide is true and mOpenFlag is set (then exit and pickup sound). While the door is closed, nothing happens and bl stays true, so the ball can roll into and through the closed 2x2 door. In 1.8 a closed exit is solid (bl=false). Exits are mid-level in levels 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10. If the ball is inside the door when it finishes opening, the next collision test ends the level.

testTile does not strip the 0x80 redraw flag. 1.01 masks only the water bit (tile & ~0x40; bytecode bipush -65/iand), so any tile carrying 0x80 matches no case and counts as empty. 1.8 masks both bits. The 13x8 buffer is cleaned by cleanBuffer(true) right before update (BounceCanvas.java:317-318), so this matters for two kinds of tiles. (a) Hoop tiles rewritten earlier in the same update: harmless, they become passable anyway in 1.01. (b) Tiles outside the buffer that the ball still touches during a step: rows below tileY+7 (centre ≥ ~89-91, and more with fast falls) and rows above tileY (via the y<0 path). These tiles can carry a stale 0x80: moving-spike tiles (10|0x80; in 1.01 these stay set because of mMODrawFlag), the exit top-left tile marked while the door opens (BounceCanvas.java:362-364), and tiles under the ball at a death site after respawning on another screen. On such tiles a moving spike does not pop the ball, an open exit does not trigger, and a brick does not block. Example: level 9, spike column (41,10)-(43,18) seen from window rows 7-14.

Vertical screen flip at the left map edge misplaces the ball when divisorLine != 156. The left-edge non-scroll branch is taken when tileX-(13-divisorLine/12)==0. That state arises with divisorLine<156 after the camera has scrolled left to the edge from a scroll-mode start or flip. Example: level 2 starts in scroll mode with tileX=3, and scrolling to the edge gives tileX=3, divisorLine=120. The flip resets to tileX=0, divisorLine=156. 1.8 converts the ball's buffer x correctly: xPos>divisorLine ? xPos-divisorLine : xPos-divisorLine+156. 1.01 only handles xPos>divisorLine. A ball left of the divisor keeps its old xPos, which puts it (156-divisorLine) px too far left, 36 px in the example, possibly inside a wall. With xPos==divisorLine the error is divisorLine px.

Horizontal buffer wrap of xPos does not adjust scrollOffset. In 1.8, when xPos wraps by ±156, scrollOffset (the trigger testScroll uses to resume scrolling at map edges) is shifted by 156 when it lies near the wrap boundary (scrollOffset-10>156+size, or scrollOffset-size<10). 1.01 leaves scrollOffset unchanged, so the point where scrolling resumes differs when scrollOffset is in about [16,22) or [16,26).

Moving-spike redraw throttle (mMODrawFlag). In 1.01, updateMovingSpikeObj marks a spike's swept tiles dirty only if that spike was drawn since the last update (drawTile case 10 sets the flag; the flag is cleared after marking). In 1.8 the swept tiles of every spike are marked every step. Spike movement, bounds and collision geometry are identical. Effects in 1.01: (1) a spike that leaves the 13x8 buffer and comes back while the camera is still is not redrawn: it is invisible or stale until a scroll column, a flip or the ball redraws its tiles; (2) its off-buffer tiles keep a stale 0x80 (see the testTile mask entry).
differences.baseline: TileCanvas.java:239-300 (unconditional marking at 270-297), drawTile case 10 at 485-502
differences.thisVersion: TileCanvas.java:210, 359, 372 (flag field and init), 425-458 (conditional marking), 649-651 (set in drawTile)

differences.what: mOpenExitFlag is not cleared on level completion. 1.8 clears it in the mExitFlag block; 1.01 does not. In normal play the flag is already cleared once the door finishes opening (mOpenFlag → mExitPos=-1, mOpenExitFlag=false at BounceCanvas.java:356-358, same in 1.8), so no observable difference.

Left soft key does nothing in game. In 1.01 only the right soft key (-7) opens the main menu; -6 and -5 are ignored. In 1.8 both -6 and -7 open the menu, and -5 is ignored. Number keys, cheat codes (7-8-7-8-9 then 8 for invincibility or 9 for level select; keys 1 and 3 change level) and game actions are identical.

No hideNotify and no resetDirections. 1.8 pauses on hide (incoming call): it clears the held direction bits (Ball.resetDirections) and shows the main menu, using mIncomingCall to skip its own menu or level transitions. 1.01 has neither, so the game keeps running while hidden and held keys are not cleared.
differences.thisVersion: absent (BounceCanvas.java ends at 537; Ball.java has no resetDirections)

differences.what: MIDlet lifecycle. 1.01 builds BounceUI in the MIDlet constructor. Its pauseApp stops the game timer, rewrites both RMS records (best level, best score) and calls notifyPaused. startApp does not restart the timer, so after a system pause the game stays frozen until the player opens the menu (right soft key) and picks Continue. destroyApp calls notifyDestroyed itself. In 1.8, BounceUI is built lazily in startApp, pauseApp is empty, destroyApp null-checks, and BounceUI calls notifyDestroyed. The RMS layout is identical: store 'bounceRMS', record 1 = 1 byte best level, record 2 = 8 bytes of decimal digits of the best score (BounceUI.java:198-308 vs 199-309).
BounceUI STATE_GAME_STARTING constant is 5 instead of 4. It is only compared with itself ('New game' guard), so there is no behavioural effect. Menus, forms and commands are otherwise identical.

Hoop sound is missing on the second hoop half. For tiles 24, 16, 22 and 14 (right half of horizontal hoops, bottom half of vertical hoops) 1.01 collects the ring silently; 1.8 plays up.ott. 1.01 also plays sounds immediately inside the switch, while 1.8 defers one sound to the end of testTile (no audible difference).

Sound files. All are Nokia Smart Messaging OTT played with com.nokia.mid.sound.Sound type 1, at 125 bpm. pop.ott is byte-identical. pickup.ott: 1.01 = G (default octave) 1/16, C(scale3) 1/8; 1.8 = C3 1/8, G2 1/16, C3 1/8. up.ott (hoop): 1.01 = pause 1/32, C3, C2, E2, F2, G2, C3 (all 1/32); 1.8 = C3, E2, G2, C3 (all 1/16).

Sprite sheet objects_nm.png (48x72, 12x12 cells). Only cell col 0, row 3 differs: the static spike (tileImages[2..9]: spikes in 4 orientations, dry and wet). 1.01 draws it as a dark blue-grey thorn; 1.8 as a red, orange and yellow thorn with black outline. The opaque silhouette is identical, and spike collision uses fixed rectangles anyway. All other 23 cells are pixel-identical.

Language files. lang.xx (English) differs only in string 12 (HIGH_SCORES): 'High scores' in 1.01, 'High score' in 1.8. lang.de string 12: 'Höchstpunkte' in 1.01, 'Punkterekord' in 1.8. The language sets differ: 1.01 has de, es-ES, fr, it, nl-NL, pt-PT, tr-TR, xx; 1.8 has da-DK, de, fi-FI, is-IS, no-NO, sv, xx. Local.class logic is identical (only access modifiers differ).

Minor items with no effect on step logic. 1.01 does not null the ball in createNewLevel (1.8 BounceCanvas.java:86) and has no gc in createBufferFocused (1.8 :96). n3/2 and mWidth/2 instead of >>1 (same for positive values). Level stream is opened outside the try, and there is no error println (TileCanvas.java:280-281 vs 124-126, 153). loadSound prints on failure (BounceCanvas.java:531). Bounce.DEBUG=true is unused. Unused fields mState, mRedrawAll and mCDEdgeFlag.

diffs.classMap: Not obfuscated, and the class names match the baseline one to one: Bounce=Bounce (MIDlet), Ball=Ball, BounceCanvas=BounceCanvas, BounceConst=BounceConst, BounceUI=BounceUI, Local=Local, Profile=Profile, TileCanvas=TileCanvas, TileCanvas$GameTimer=TileCanvas$GameTimer. Local.class and Profile.class are byte-identical to 1.8. TileCanvas$GameTimer has the same bytecode (Timer.schedule(this, 0, 30L), so 30 ms); only its LineNumberTable differs. Some fields were renamed, which changes nothing at runtime: Ball.ballSize->mBallSize, Ball.ballImage->mBallImage, BounceCanvas.mExitFlag->mLeaveGame, TileCanvas.buffer/bufferGraphics->mGameBuffer/mGameGraphics, mStartPosX/Y->mStartCol/mStartRow, mTopLeftTileCol/Row->mTopLeftExitTileCol/Row, BounceUI.getGameData/setGameData->loadGameData/saveGameData. Line references below are to the CFR files under .../jars/<version>/cfr/com/nokia/mid/appl/boun/. Every method was checked against the baseline by a normalized javap -c -p diff. After that diff, only these methods differ: Ball.<init>, Ball.setRespawn; Bounce.destroyApp; BounceCanvas.createNewLevel, createBufferFocused, resetGame(int), run, paint2Buffer (0-x became -x, same result), plus new methods resetGame(int,int), resetTiles, tileNotSavedAsActive; TileCanvas.loadLevel, drawTile (exit case only), createExitTileObject; BounceUI.<clinit>, displayMainMenu, displayGameOver, commandAction, load/saveGameData, plus new methods displayNewGameMenu and gameOver. Ball.update, testTile, collisionDetection, square/triangle/thin/edgeCollide, enlarge/shrink/popBall, redirectBall, dirtyTiles, all of TileCanvas scrolling/cleanBuffer/updateMovingSpikeObj/loadTileImages, screenFlip, keyPressed/keyReleased, the cheat codes, hideNotify, checkData and paint have the same bytecode as 1.8.

differences.what: Every spawn and respawn puts the ball 1 pixel higher (yPos is one less) than 1.8. This covers level start, respawn after death, and resume.
differences.baseline: BounceCanvas.java:122 creates new Ball((col-tileX)*12+(size>>1), (row-tileY)*12+(size>>1), ...), where size=16 if mBallSize==1 else 12. A small ball's centre is at row*12+6, a big ball's at row*12+8 (screen-relative).
differences.thisVersion: BounceCanvas.java:141-143: n8 = n - tileX*12; n9 = n2 - tileY*12 - 1; new Ball(n8, n9, size, this). The callers pass n = col*12+(size>>1) and n2 = row*12+(size>>1) (createNewLevel :111, respawn :339), so the centre y is (row-tileY)*12 + size/2 - 1. Confirmed in bytecode (iconst_1 isub at createBufferFocused offset 191). X is unchanged. Example: on level 1 (start col 2, row 1, brick ceiling above) the small ball now starts 1 px inside the ceiling tile and only drops free on frame 3. It also reaches the floor 1 px later than in 1.8, so every later step is offset.

differences.what: The big-ball unstick nudge at spawn was removed.
differences.baseline: BounceCanvas.java:124-134: if the spawned ball is big (mBallSize==1) and collisionDetection(x,y) fails, it tries x-4, then y-4, then both, and moves the ball to the first spot that fits. These collisionDetection calls also run testTile side effects (items, spikes, deflators, mCDRampFlag/mCDRubberFlag, globalBallX/Y).
differences.thisVersion: BounceCanvas.java:115-147 makes no collision test and no adjustment at spawn, for any size. With the shipped levels no level start triggers the nudge (big starts L03 (52,2), L05 (32,32), L11 (142,37) all have free tiles right and below). The only checkpoint where it could fire is L11 (143,45), which is ringed by deflator tiles. So in practice only the 1 px offset above shows up, but a rules.js that copies 1.8 must not nudge for 1.9.

differences.what: The spawn API changed from tile coordinates to pixel centre plus size plus speeds, and the respawn size moved from a canvas field into the Ball. The behaviour is the same.
differences.baseline: createBufferFocused(col,row) (BounceCanvas.java:95-136) uses the camera tests col*12+6 <64 and > W*12-64, tileX = col-6, tileY = row/7*7. Respawn size is the canvas flag mBallSize, set by loadLevel (TileCanvas.java:129) and by Ball.setRespawn (Ball.java:85). On death it calls createBufferFocused(respawnX, respawnY) (BounceCanvas.java:323), which also calls setRespawn again (:123). There is also a Runtime.gc() (:96), and createNewLevel sets mBall=null (:86).
differences.thisVersion: createBufferFocused(px,py,size,xSpeed,ySpeed) (BounceCanvas.java:115-147) uses the tests px<64 and px>W*12-64, with tileX=px/12-6 and tileY=(py/12)/7*7. For whole-number columns these give the same camera as 1.8 for both sizes. Ball.respawnSize is set in setRespawn (Ball.java:82-86). On death, run() saves respawnX/Y/Size, rebuilds the ball, and restores them (BounceCanvas.java:336-342). createNewLevel calls setRespawn(startCol,startRow) (:112). The new ball's xSpeed and ySpeed are set from the arguments (0,0 except on resume). There is no gc, and mBall is never nulled.

differences.what: The level header's start-size byte is decoded differently.
differences.baseline: TileCanvas.java:129 stores the raw byte in mBallSize. Ball.java:71-79 maps 0 to 12 and 1 to 16; any other value leaves the size at 0 with no image.
differences.thisVersion: TileCanvas.java:127-128 sets mStartBallSize = (byte==0 ? 12 : 16). Ball.java:72-79 treats 12 as small and anything else as 16. All 11 shipped level files are identical to 1.8 and use only 0 or 1, so nothing changes.

differences.what: Exit door drawing: all four 2x2 exit tiles are now redrawn while the door opens, each clipped to its own 12x12 cell. The unused bottom-right exit coordinates were dropped.
differences.baseline: BounceCanvas.java:357-359 marks only tileMap[topRow][topCol] |= 0x80 each opening step. drawTile case 9 (TileCanvas.java:478-483) draws the whole 24x24 exit image unclipped. createExitTileObject(col,row,col+1,row+2,img) is at TileCanvas.java:132, 925-935.
differences.thisVersion: BounceCanvas.java:376-387 marks (r,c), (r,c+1), (r+1,c) and (r+1,c+1). drawTile case 9 (TileCanvas.java:477-485) calls setClip(x,y,12,12), draws the image, then resets the clip to the buffer size. createExitTileObject(col,row,img) is at TileCanvas.java:131, 926-934. mExitPos = x-(tileCol-exitCol)*12+11 gives the same value from any exit tile, and cleanBuffer draws in column order, so the opening timing (6 openExit steps, mOpenFlag, mExitPos=-1) is the same.

differences.what: There is no longer a black clear frame after a level is completed. mClearScreenFlag is never set to true anywhere, so the clear branch of paint() is dead code.
differences.baseline: BounceCanvas.java:394 sets mClearScreenFlag = true after displayLevelComplete(), so paint() (:258-261) fills the screen black once.

differences.what: Game over now goes through a new BounceUI.gameOver(), which sets mState=3 and invalidates the saved game. The win path (mLevelNum>=11 after a level is completed) still calls displayGameOver() directly, which no longer sets mState=3.
differences.baseline: BounceUI.java:129-131: displayGameOver() sets mState=3 for both death and win (called from BounceCanvas.java:320 and :390). After winning, Continue (shown because mBestLevel>1) calls resetGame(mCanvas.mLevelNum): level 11 with 3 lives and score 0 (BounceUI.java:168-175).
differences.thisVersion: BounceCanvas.java:333 calls mUI.gameOver() (BounceUI.java:366-370: mState=3, mSavedValid=-16, displayGameOver). displayGameOver (BounceUI.java:160-177) does not touch mState. Win path: BounceCanvas.java:416-418. After winning, mState stays 1, so Continue calls displayGame(false,...). run() then sees mLoadLevelFlag and loads level 11 with the current lives, score and ring count, not 3/0.

differences.what: New rule for when the main menu shows Continue.
differences.thisVersion: BounceUI.java:95: shown if mState==1 || mSavedValid==-6 (a valid saved snapshot was loaded from RMS at startup).

differences.what: Continue now resumes a saved snapshot instead of restarting a level.
differences.baseline: BounceUI.java:168-175: if mState!=1, Continue calls resetGame(mState==3 ? mCanvas.mLevelNum : mBestLevel). That is a fresh level with 3 lives, score 0 and 0 rings.
differences.thisVersion: BounceUI.java:201-210: if mState==1 it resumes the current game. Otherwise, if mSavedValid==-6, it calls BounceCanvas.resetGame(savedGlobalX+size/2, savedGlobalY+size/2) (BounceCanvas.java:85-103). That sets level, rings, lives and score from the save, reloads the level, and calls resetTiles() (:574-631). resetTiles sets every crystal (7), extra-life ball (29) and unpassed hoop tile (13-16, 21-24) that is not in the saved active list to its collected form (0, or 17-20/25-28), keeping the 0x40 water bit. It sets mLevelDisCntr=120, sets the saved respawn tile to 8|water only if respawnX!=startCol && respawnY!=startRow (&& where || was meant; visual only), places the ball (1 px above the saved centre) with the saved size and xSpeed/ySpeed, restores respawnX/Y and the speed, gravity and jump bonus counters, then sets mSavedTiles=null and mState=1. Not restored: jumpOffset, grounded/ramp/rubber flags, slideCntr, direction, moving-spike offsets, exit-opening progress, the saved tileX/tileY/xPos/yPos (read but unused), mInvincible and mCheat. The camera is recomputed from the ball position. respawnSize becomes the ball's size at save time, not its size when the crystal was taken.

differences.what: New Game now opens a level-select list once the player has reached a level above 1.
differences.baseline: BounceUI.java:176-181: New Game always calls displayGame(true,1) (with mState=4 and mNewBestScore=false).
differences.thisVersion: BounceUI.java:211-220: if mBestLevel>1 it calls displayNewGameMenu() (BounceUI.java:114-127). That is an IMPLICIT List titled with Local string 16 ('New game'), with items Local 14 ('Level %U') for 1..mBestLevel and a Back command. Selecting an item calls displayGame(true, index+1) (BounceUI.java:196-197): that level with 3 lives and score 0. This path does not reset mNewBestScore, so a stale 'New high score!' can appear on the next game-over screen. If mBestLevel<=1 the behaviour is as in 1.8.

differences.what: New record store layout. 'bounceRMS' now has 3 records written with DataOutputStream, instead of 2 records in digit format.
differences.baseline: BounceUI.java:199-309: the store must hold exactly 2 records, otherwise 2 records are added ([0] and 8 zero bytes) and then read. Record 1 is 1 byte (best level). Record 2 is 8 bytes, the best score as 8 decimal digits, most significant first, one per byte (0-9). setGameData(1|2) rewrites one record.
differences.thisVersion: BounceUI.java:239-364: if getNumRecords()!=3 it adds 1, 4 and 255 zero bytes and reads nothing; otherwise it reads all three. Record 1 is readByte (best level). Record 2 is readInt, big-endian (best score). Record 3 is the snapshot: byte valid (-6=0xFA valid; -16 is only ever kept in memory), byte lives, byte rings, byte level, byte ballSize (12/16), then ints score, tileX, tileY, globalBallX, globalBallY, xSpeed, ySpeed, xPos, yPos, respawnX, respawnY, speedBonusCntr, gravBonusCntr, jumpBonusCntr (65 bytes so far), then byte n, then n times (short row, short col, byte tileId) for still-active tiles of type 7, 29, 13, 14, 15, 16, 21, 22, 23 or 24, using a fixed int[40][3] buffer. An old 1.8 store (2 records) is never read again: 3 records are added on every launch, so the count is never 3.

differences.what: The game state is saved automatically on exit, and only on exit. This brings bugs that change play on the next launch.
differences.baseline: Bounce.java:31-38: destroyApp stops the canvas, clears the display and calls System.gc(). Nothing is saved.
differences.thisVersion: Bounce.java:31-38: destroyApp calls mUI.saveGameData(3) after stop() (line 34) and no longer calls System.gc(). saveGameData(3) (BounceUI.java:309-356) always writes valid=-6 and never checks mState. (a) Exiting after a Game Over saves lives=-1, so the next launch offers Continue and resumes at the death spot with numLives=-1, which is one extra life. (b) Exiting from the level-complete or win screen saves the next level number together with the old level's ball position and ring count. (c) More than 40 active collectibles throws ArrayIndexOutOfBounds, which is silently caught, so nothing is saved. Level 11 has 50 at its start; levels 1-10 have 15-35. (d) If no game was played, mBall is null, the NPE is caught, and the old save is kept.

differences.what: Some debug output and memory housekeeping were removed.
differences.baseline: TileCanvas.java:153 prints 'Error trying to read file' on IOException. BounceCanvas.java:86 sets mBall=null during level load, :96 calls Runtime.gc() on every (re)spawn. Bounce.java:37 calls System.gc().
differences.thisVersion: TileCanvas.java:152 has an empty catch, and the mBall=null and gc calls are gone. BounceConst gains only compile-time constants (ID_WATER_MASK, RMS_*, GAME_DATA_VALID/INVALID, STATE_*). BounceUI loses its private static RESTART_* booleans (<clinit>).

differences.what: Different language packs ship with the game. The English fallback is unchanged.
differences.baseline: lang.xx, lang.da-DK, lang.de, lang.fi-FI, lang.is-IS, lang.no-NO, lang.sv
differences.thisVersion: lang.xx (byte-identical to 1.8), lang.tl-PH, lang.vi-VN, lang.zh-CN, lang.zh-TW. Same 21-string table and loader (Local.class identical). The file is chosen by exact match of microedition.locale, falling back to lang.xx.

diffs.notes:
Who built it and when: Nokia, two days after 1.8 (jar entries dated Dec 12 2002 vs Dec 10 2002). The manifest's Created-By changed from '1.3.1.02 (Hewlett-Packard Co.)' to '1.3.1_02 (Sun Microsystems Inc.)'. It is the same unobfuscated com.nokia.mid.appl.boun source tree with some fields renamed to an m-prefix style, not a third-party port.

The per-frame step is unchanged. Build. This is a genuine Nokia build: MIDlet-Vendor Nokia, package com.nokia.mid.appl.boun, Nokia UI API (FullCanvas, DirectGraphics, Sound). The classes are obfuscated (a-f), class-file major version 45, JAR entries dated 2004-01-23. The manifest says "Created-By: 14.0.1 (Oracle Corporation)", which suggests the JAR was repackaged later.

Screen layout is the same as 1.8: 128x128 full canvas, a 156x96 tile ring buffer, play area at y 0-96, HUD at y 97-128 (background 0x0853AA). Sounds are Nokia OTT tones played with Sound(byte[],1).

Unchanged per-step code (byte-identical after renaming): collisionDetection and its tile walk, the square and triangle pixel tests with the 12x12/16x16 masks, enlarge/shrink, popBall (lives-1, 5-tick pop), scoring (ring 500, crystal 200, extra life 1000 up to max 5, level 5000), gravity/water constants (80/4, 38/3, 42/6, -30/-2), jump -67 plus offsets, x acceleration 6 / friction 4 / cap 50 or 100, the 300-tick bonuses, the screen wrap at 156, scrollBuffer, testScroll, moving-spike movement, exit opening, and the order of the step in run(). The cheat codes 7878-8 and 7878-9-9 and the 1/3 level keys are also unchanged.

Not behavioural:
- The start ball size is now carried as 12/16 instead of 0/1 (b.java:126-127, e.java:72-79), and the respawn size moved from the canvas into the Ball (e.java:82-86, d.java:332-338). Both are equivalent to 1.8.
- The camera choice in createBufferFocused gives the same result for integer tiles.

Fixes in 1.21: the screenFlip right clamp, overdraw by the exit image, HUD rings running off-screen, level 11 now part of normal play, and the best level capped at 11.

New quirks in 1.21:
- The game runs during the Level-complete screen, so the start of the next level depends on wall-clock time: spike phase and banner timer.
- Spawns are 1 px inside ceilings.
- The saved-checkpoint restore uses && instead of ||.
- A saved game remembers the ball size at save time, not at the checkpoint.

For a step-exact rules.js port of 1.21, change these from 1.8: the minimum fall speed of 10, the ceiling bounce (-vy)>>1, the new redirectBall formulas, the ramp flag on brick contact, grounded=false on the gravity pickup, the thinCollide / edgeCollide(14,18,22,26) / spike hit boxes, the -1 px spawn and no nudge, the screenFlip clamp, the level count of 11, the level-11 tile at row 42 col 91 = 97, and the FIRE and '#' cheats.

diffs.notes:
1.24 is a Nokia rework, not a third-party port: vendor Nokia, package com.nokia.mid.appl.boun, compiled with Sun JDK 1.4.2_02, obfuscated, dated 2004-08-16. The tile ids, collision masks, gravity, jump and speed constants, scoring (ring 500, checkpoint 200, life 1000, exit 5000), 3 starting lives with a cap of 5, the 300-step bonuses, the moving-spike update, findSpikeIndex, edgeCollide, squareCollide/triangleCollide maths, the bonus bar and the cheat sequences are all the same as 1.8.

The engine was rewritten around world coordinates. The ball's position is in world pixels, the camera is separate, and the ball has no xOffset or 156-px wrap. That rewrite brings changes to:
- the ball update: ceiling speed, the new minimum downward speed of 10, ramp redirection, enlarge/shrink, the big-ball spawn position, and the pop length of 7 steps;
- collision: early exit on the first blocking tile, smaller thin-tile and spike boxes, and tile 1 setting the ramp flag;
- the camera: earlier vertical flips with almost no hysteresis, different framing on rows that are multiples of 7, and a right-edge clamp at 12W-144 that hides the last 16 px of each level.

So the per-step logic is NOT the same as 1.8. A 1.24 mode in rules.js needs its own ball and collision code. 1.21's CFR still has the 1.8-style screenFlip and ring-buffer code (1.21 d.java:169-178), so this rewrite seems to be new in 1.24 (worth checking against the 1.21 report).

Screen layout: hard-coded 128x128 only. The play view is 128x96 (clip 0,0,128,96), drawn from a 156x96 tile ring buffer at offset af, and the HUD fills 0..128 x 97..128. No other resolutions are supported.

Sound: the same three Nokia OTT tone files, played through com.nokia.mid.sound.Sound(byte[], 1).play(1), unchanged.

Baseline bugs fixed in 1.24:
- 1.8 ends after level 10, so level 11 is normally unreachable.
- 1.8's screenFlip right-edge clamp can move the ball 336 px (BounceCanvas.java:182).
- 1.8's HUD cannot show more than about 11 ring icons.
- 1.8's Local.replace only replaces the first occurrence.

Bugs introduced in 1.24:
- The camera never shows the last 16 px of a level: (W+1)*12-156 in e.java:594-596, versus W*12-156 in the recentre at c.java:131.
- The timer is restarted under the level-complete form, so the next level runs without input (a.java:186).
- Restoring a game: the && when setting back the active checkpoint (c.java:93), the respawn size becomes the current size, and a big ball moves 1 px on restore.
- The record store adds 3 new records whenever the count is not 3, so it never reads an older 2-record store and keeps growing it.
- The flip test uses a fixed 6 px for both ball sizes.

differences.what: createBufferFocused, left-end branch (start or checkpoint column <= 4): the camera's right edge is set to 132 instead of 128, so the window is 132 px wide (leftDrawEdge 0 .. rightDrawEdge 132). The middle branch (15..143) and right branch (28..156) are still 128 wide. The wider window lasts through scrolling until a later screenFlip or respawn takes another branch. Once scrolling starts (ball at buffer x 64, same as 1.8), the ball sits at L+64 and the right edge at ball+68 instead of ball+64. Levels 1 and 7 start in this branch.

screenFlip, 'camera parked at left end' branch (!scrollFlag && tileX-(13-divisorLine/12)==0): this branch also sets the right edge to 132 instead of 128. The other branches are unchanged: right end 28/156; scrolling 14+n2/142+n2 with ball at 78+n2.

Knock-on effect of the 132-wide window on the scroll state machine. The scrollBuffer and testScroll code is identical; only its inputs change. Scrolling stops at the right map edge with the ball 4 px further left: scrollFlag goes false at ball world x of about 12W-68 instead of 12W-64. The resume point (scrollOffset = rightDrawEdge-64) is then 4 px right of the ball. After resuming, the window sits at ball-68 .. ball+64, so the left-end stop also happens about 4-5 px earlier (own camera re-implementation, camsim.py: stop at step 76 vs 77, left stop at ball 67 vs 62). In those 4-5 px bands scrollFlag differs, so a vertical screen flip there takes a different screenFlip branch (parked vs scrolling). This changes tileX, divisorLine, the edges and the ball's buffer xPos afterwards. The world position is normally kept by every branch, except the shared clamp bug in the scrolling branch ('n2 += (tileX - mTileMapWidth - 13 - 1) * 12'), which teleports the ball when it flips while scrolling with ball column >= W-7. In this window state the port takes the non-buggy parked branch in the last ~4 px where 1.8 would still be scrolling.

Exit opening starts earlier in the 132-wide state. run() starts the 6-step exit opening (openExit, +4 px per step; tile 9 stays solid until mOpenFlag) only when mExitPos lies within [leftDrawEdge, rightDrawEdge]. The test code is identical, but the right edge is 4 px further out, so the exit begins opening up to 4 px (about one step at 5 px/step) earlier relative to the ball. In camsim.py an exit at world x 371 became visible at step 54 instead of 55.

Soft keys: key codes -4 and -1 (Siemens right/left soft keys) now also leave the game for the main menu, as -6/-7 already did. On a Nokia keypad -1/-4 would be UP/RIGHT, but on the Siemens target they are the soft keys.

Siemens joystick codes are remapped to number keys before getGameAction, in keyPressed only: -61→'4', -62→'6', -59→'2', -60→'8', -23→'5'. keyReleased is not remapped, so release relies on the device's own getGameAction for these codes. The remap happens in the default branch after the switch, so joystick-down (-60→56) never feeds the 7-8-7-8-9 cheat sequence. The cheats (78789 then 8 = invincible, then 9 = level skip with keys 1/3) are otherwise unchanged; their confirmation sounds go through Player.start in try/catch.

Sound API: MMAPI Players created from /sounds/*.mid ('audio/midi') replace com.nokia.mid.sound.Sound built from /sounds/*.ott. Playback is player.start() inside try/catch instead of play(1). loadSound returns a shared field (aa), so if one Player fails to load, the previously loaded Player is returned in its place. There is no fallback beep (1.8 played Sound(1000 Hz, 500 ms) x3 on load failure).

Losing a life now also vibrates for 100 ms via the Siemens API com.siemens.mp.game.Vibrator.triggerVibrator(100). The call is in the same try as the pop sound and only runs when not invincible. On a non-Siemens VM this would throw NoClassDefFoundError, which the catch(Exception) does not catch.

Screen layout for 132x176. Off-screen buffer is 132x176 (was 128x128). /icons/head.png (132x48 BOUNCE banner) is drawn at (0,0) every frame. The 96-px play area is drawn at y=48 (was y=0). Level label at (44,132), was (44,84). HUD bar fillRect(0,144,132,32) colour 0x0853AA, was (0,97,128,32), so there is no 1-px gap row. Lives at y=147 (was 99). Remaining-hoop icons at y=160 (was 112). Score at (68,148) (was (64,100)). Bonus bar fillRect(1,176-3*v/30,5,176), was 128-based. Only the play strip uses the camera window; when the window is 128 wide, the rightmost 4 screen columns show a not-yet-refreshed buffer column, or stale frame pixels when L=28/R=156.
The HUD shows at most 11 remaining-hoop icons; 1.8 draws mTotalNumRings - numRings icons with no limit.
New HUD decoration: an 8x5 down-arrow image (/icons/66.png, static field a.h) is drawn at (124,169), anchor 0, whenever the HUD is repainted.

Tile images are loaded as separate PNGs (/icons/<col><row>[variant].png) instead of being cut from the objects_nm.png sprite sheet. Flipped and rotated hoop/spike variants are pre-rendered files (031/033/035, X51-X57), not runtime DirectGraphics transforms. The 16x16 large ball is /icons/30.png instead of being composed from four mirrored quarters of cell (3,0) (createLargeBallImage was removed). The background-filled variants use Image.createImage plus fillRect plus drawRegion.

Runtime flips and rotations (manipulateImage) now draw with drawRegion into Image.createImage(w,h), an opaque white mutable image, instead of a transparent DirectUtils.createImage(w,h,0). The transform codes map correctly (MIRROR, MIRROR_ROT180, ROT180, ROT270=Nokia 90 CCW, ROT90=Nokia 270). However, transparent pixels become white. This is visible on rubber ramps 34/35/37 (rotations of 02.png, which has alpha), where white replaces the sky/water background in the empty half. Other affected sources (31/24/32/22/13/23 and the bg-filled ramps) are opaque.

Sprite art differs from the 1.8 sheet cells (compared per pixel against each cell plus the transform 1.8 applies). Identical: 02 (rubber ramp) and 12 (rubber brick). Colour quantisation only (<=2 levels): 03, 11, 22, 32. Small shading edits: 01 popped ball, 13 moving spike, 20 small ball, 21 life, 23 exit, 33 extra life, 34 used checkpoint. Redrawn: 00 ramp (red brick → orange/gold), 10 brick (red → orange/gold block), 04 checkpoint (crystal → floppy disk), 14 HUD hoop counter (ring → key), 30 large ball (16x16 hand-drawn), 31 deflator (recoloured, made opaque), 24 inflator (made opaque with sky colour baked in). The hoop halves X5/X51-X57 are hand-made and differ from exact flips of the 1.8 cells by 25-44 px. The spike variants are not exact transforms either: 035 equals a CCW rotation where 1.8 uses CW, and 031/033 differ by about 22 px. Unused extras: 00a/10a/14a/ball.png (exact copies of 1.8 cells (0,0),(1,0),(1,4),(2,0)), 04a, 032, null.png, and a modified objects_nm.png (15 cells differ from 1.8, never loaded).

New or changed full-screen images. bouncesplash.png is 132x176 and reads 'SIEMENS x65 / BOUNCE / iceman345 IHT (c) 2005 www.iceman.ru' (1.8: 128x128). head.png is new (132x48 banner). coloricons.png is new (7 icons of 16x16; the first 6 are used for the menu). nokiagames.png and icon.png are identical.

Every note is flattened into one octave (MIDI 48-59, C3-B3). The OTT tones use scale-2/scale-3 notes an octave or more apart (e.g. hoop C(s3) E(s2) G(s2) C(s3)), so the pitch contour changes.

diffs.notes:
Who made it: a third-party port for the Siemens x65 series (CX65/S65/M65, 132x176). The About text, splash and Siemens Vibrator API show this, as do MMAPI MIDI sounds and the Siemens soft-key and joystick codes. Credited to iceman345 [IHT], 2005.
- It was recompiled and re-obfuscated. Loops have the condition at the top, local-variable slots differ, and the classes are preverified (StackMap, class version 45.3).
- The JAR was later repacked with a JDK 14 jar tool.

How the comparison was done: every method of both builds was disassembled with javap. Member names were mapped to 1.8's, local variables renumbered, and methods compared as instruction sequences and as multisets of basic blocks (script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/9e293dcf-c6a7-5416-93b2-b9c9546fbcbb/scratchpad/work/versions/v1.8-132x176/bcdiff.py).

Identical, or differing only in block layout or local-variable slots:
- Ball: update, testTile apart from the sound call, collisionDetection, square/triangle/thin/edge collide, redirect, enlarge/shrink, respawn, directions, paint/dirtyTiles. testTile's tile 0 now falls to the switch default, which is equivalent. update's ±1 step now has an i2b cast, which has no effect.
- TileCanvas: loadLevel, createMovingObj, updateMovingSpikeObj, findSpikeIndex, drawTile, cleanBuffer, createNewBuffer, scrollBuffer, testScroll, createExitTileObject/openExit, rectCollide.
- BounceCanvas: run() (step order unchanged), resetGame, createNewLevel, checkData, add2Score, zeroString, keyReleased, hideNotify, paint.
- BounceUI record-store code and Local.
- Timer: Timer.schedule(…, 0, 30 ms), same as 1.8.
- Level files 001-011 are byte-identical to 1.8.

The only per-step logic change is the camera's right edge, 132 instead of 128, in the left-end branches of createBufferFocused and screenFlip. It moves the right-end scroll stop and resume points and the left-end stop after a resume by about 4 px. It can flip which screenFlip branch runs in those narrow bands, and it lets the exit start opening about one step earlier. The ball's world position stays the same except through the screenFlip clamp bug that 1.8 also has.

Bugs kept from 1.8:
- screenFlip clamp: n2 += (tileX - W - 13 - 1)*12, which should be (tileX-(W-14))*12. It teleports the ball when it flips while scrolling within 7 columns of the right edge.
- At xPos == divisorLine, screenFlip and collisionDetection disagree.
- tileY is used instead of divTileY in update's water check.

Bugs added by the port:
- White backgrounds on runtime-rotated transparent sprites (rubber ramps 34/35/37).
- The 4-px stale strip at the right of the 132-px screen when the window is 128 wide.
- No Back/Exit soft command on the main menu.
- Vibrator call crashes on non-Siemens VMs.
- Shared-field Player loading.

- bestfit.py: finds the closest flip/rotation for the pre-rendered hoop and spike PNGs.
- montage.png: side-by-side picture of 1.8 vs port tiles.
- sounds.py: decodes the OTT and MIDI sound files.
- lang.py: dumps lang.* strings.
- camsim.py: my own re-implementation of the 1.8 camera code, comparing a 128 vs 132 right edge; none of the jar's code was run.

playDifferencesFrom18: Game timer 40 ms instead of 30 ms. The step sequence is unchanged, but the game runs 25% slower in real time.
No +/-150 clamp on xSpeed/ySpeed before the vertical loop, so stacked rubber jumps, jump bonus and ramp redirects can go past 150.

A landing does not end the vertical loop (javap: goto 854 = i++, where 1.8 has goto 946 = loop exit). The loop bound |ySpeed|/10 is re-read, so the ball can rebound upward in the same step. That clears grounded, so there is no jump on that landing.
Ceiling rebound ySpeed is 6 instead of 20, so the rest of that step's vertical loop is skipped.
When a big ball leaves water, ySpeed is halved with idiv (rounds toward 0) instead of ishr; this differs for odd negative speeds.
No wall bounce: when blocked horizontally with the ramp flag set, xSpeed is kept (1.8 sets xSpeed = -(xSpeed>>1)).
Plain ramps 30-33 redirect at full speed (x=y, y=x or x=-y, y=-x); 1.8 halves both on 30-33.
collisionDetection with the centre above the buffer (y<0) snaps the mask to -12*(|y|/12+1), so hits above the top edge are tested at the wrong height.

No hoop rims (no edgeCollide). Active hoops 21-24 always collect. 13-16 collect for the small ball and are solid for the big one. Collected 17-20 are solid only for the big ball; 25-28 can be passed through.
Collecting a hoop writes plain 145-156, which drops the tile's 0x40 water bit (wet hoops in levels 3, 5, 7, 8, 11 turn into air).
The closed exit door (tile 9) can be passed through; 1.8 makes it solid until it is open.

testTile masks only 0x40 (bipush -65), not the 0x80 dirty bit. Any tile with a stale 0x80 counts as empty: off-buffer moving-spike tiles, the exit tile while it opens, tiles left behind after a respawn elsewhere.
A vertical screen flip in the parked left-edge state with divisorLine<156 leaves a ball left of the divisor at its old xPos, (156-divisorLine) px too far left.
When xPos wraps by 156, scrollOffset is not shifted, so the point where scrolling resumes at map edges differs.
otherDifferences: No BounceConst class; constants are inlined in Ball, TileCanvas and BounceCanvas. Field names myParent/myBall.
Moving-spike redraw is throttled by mMODrawFlag (drawing only, but it is what leaves stale 0x80 on spike tiles).
No hoop sound on the second half of a hoop (tiles 24, 16, 22, 14); different pickup.ott and up.ott tones.
The left soft key (-6) does nothing in game. There is no hideNotify pause and no resetDirections.
pauseApp stops the timer and writes RMS, and startApp does not restart it. The RMS layout is the same 2-record format as 1.8.
Static-spike sprite cell differs (blue-grey thorn); lang.xx says 'High scores'; different language set.
Same as 1.8: all 11 level files, masks, gravity/jump/speed constants, scoring, the run() step order, camera scroll code, and 10-level campaign end (mLevelNum >= 11).

synth.lineage:
One Nokia source line, plus one third-party port branched from 1.8. The evidence is file dates, shared renames and resources, and method-level bytecode diffs.

1. 1.01 (2 Oct 2002, 40 ms) is the earliest. It is the same unobfuscated com.nokia.mid.appl.boun code, without BounceConst.

2. 1.8 (10 Dec 2002, 30 ms) is a bug-fix release of 1.01 on the same HP toolchain. It adds the +/-150 clamp, the loop exit after a landing, the ceiling 20, the wall bounce, halved plain ramps, hoop rims, a solid closed exit, the water bit kept on hoops, the 0x80 mask, the left-flip fix and the pause-on-hide.

3. 1.9 (12 Dec 2002, 30 ms, Sun JDK) is 1.8 with fields renamed to an m-prefix style. It adds the save/resume system, a level select, the -1 px spawn, removal of the nudge, and clipped exit drawing. Ball physics are byte-identical to 1.8.

4. 1.12 (14 Feb 2003, 30 ms) continues 1.9: the same renames, save code, resetTiles and -1 spawn. It adds the new redirectBall, the (-v)>>1 ceiling, the 11-level campaign, the FIRE cheat, spike state in the save, and the 8-px HUD ring row with a new sprite sheet. That sheet is byte-identical in 1.12, 1.18, 1.21 and 1.24. 1.12 also returns to the HP toolchain.

5. 1.18 (10 Oct 2003) is the first obfuscated build and switches to 40 ms. A normalised opcode diff against 1.12 shows only two Ball changes: the minimum fall speed (water check only) and the brick ramp flag. It also adds the '#' and FIRE cheats, runs the next level behind the level-complete form, re-indexes the lang files, and introduces the mState=5 bug.

6. 1.21 (23 Jan 2004) uses the same obfuscation names as 1.18, and its CFR diff is small. Changes: thinCollide, the bottom edge rims and the spike box shrink by 1-2 px; the antigravity pickup clears grounded; the minimum fall speed skips antigravity; the screenFlip clamp is fixed; Continue resets the state; directions are cleared on resume; the save gets a timestamp and DEADBEEF; one level 11 tile changes.

7. 1.24 (16 Aug 2004, Sun JDK 1.4.2) rewrites the engine in world coordinates. It inherits the 1.21-only rules (hit boxes, grounded on the antigravity pickup, minimum fall speed guard, DEADBEEF save, level 11 tile), but reverts the edgeCollide change and the -1 small-ball spawn. It adds pop 7, enlarge from 1 px, no shrink nudge, early-exit collision, and a new flip and camera.

Side branch: the 1.8 132x176 build (2005) is iceman345's Siemens port, made from the 1.8 128x128 code. It keeps 1.8's physics, RMS and lang files; adds lang.ru; widens the left-end camera to 132; and replaces the sounds, keys and sprites.

The 1.18 and 1.21 JARs were repacked later (Created-By 14.0.1 Oracle). Their class files keep their original dates.
synth.recommendation:
Make Nokia 1.8 128x128 (30 ms tick) the reference for js/rules.js. Use the 1.8 level files: they are byte-identical in 1.01-1.18 and in the port.

Why 1.8:
1. Its code is the most reliable source: unobfuscated, with original names from JD-GUI and a full CFR/javap match.
2. Its per-step code is shared exactly by 1.9 (only the spawn y differs) and by the Siemens port (only the camera width differs). The same engine therefore covers three of the eight builds and the whole Dec 2002 line.
3. It is the first build with 1.01's collision bugs fixed: passable closed exit, no hoop rims, bounce-loop rebound, ceiling 6, 0x80 mask, lost water bits.
4. It has no wall-clock-dependent behaviour. From 1.18 on, the next level runs behind the level-complete form for as many ticks as the player takes to press Continue, which a deterministic remake cannot reproduce faithfully.

What most players had cannot be settled from these JARs. The dates suggest 1.8/1.9 for the early-2003 128x128 Series 40 phones and 1.18-1.24 for 2004 handsets; confirming that needs outside evidence such as firmware dumps.

Trade-offs of 1.8 the remake inherits:
- The campaign ends after level 10. Level 11 is reachable only via Continue after Game over (3 lives, 0 points) or the cheat.
- The HUD overflows past about 11 rings on levels 9-11.
- Rare screenFlip clamp teleport near the right map edge while scrolling.
- Touch-counts spike and thin hit boxes, and a sticky ramp flag.
- No saved game.
Keep all of these in strict mode. If fixes are wanted, offer them as explicit opt-in flags, not as defaults.

If a later ruleset is wanted, make it a separate, labelled mode built as deltas on 1.8:
- 1.9: spawnYOffset -1 and no nudge.
- 1.12: also the new redirectBall, the (-v)>>1 ceiling and 11 levels.
- 1.18: also the minimum fall speed (water check only) and the brick ramp flag.
- 1.21: also the thin, edge and spike box changes, grounded cleared on the antigravity pickup, the antigravity guard on the minimum fall speed, the flip-clamp fix, the level 11 tile and 40 ms.

1.24 cannot be expressed as a delta (world coordinates, early-exit collisions, 7-step pop, new camera and flips) and would need its own engine. 1.01 is a buggy pre-release. The 132x176 build is a third-party port.
spotChecks: Timer periods, from javap of every GameTimer: ldc2_w 40 in 1.01, 1.18 (f), 1.21 (f) and 1.24 (g); 30 in 1.8, 1.9, 1.12 and the port (a$a). Confirmed. The reports disagreed on whether 40 ms affects play (1.01 and 1.21 said yes, 1.18 and 1.24 said no). The table treats it the same way everywhere: the step sequence is unchanged, but real-time speed is 25% slower.

1.01 vertical loop (javap Ball.update). 1.8 jumps to 946 (loop exit) after a landing; 1.01 jumps to 854 (i++). Ceiling: bipush -20/20 against -6/6. No clamp in 1.01: offset 415 goes straight to the loop test. Water halving: idiv at 1.01 offset 524, ishr at 1.8 offset 598. All confirmed.

1.01 testTile mask: bipush -65 iand only, where 1.8 has bipush -65 iand sipush -129 iand. Confirmed. Also confirmed in CFR: plain hoop values 145-156, no edgeCollide calls, closed exit with no else branch, full-speed plain ramps, no wall-bounce else, no scrollOffset shift, the left-edge flip branch, and soft key -6 swallowed.

Floor versus ceiling looked like a disagreement: 1.01's report says 1.8 breaks after a bounce, while 1.12/1.18 say the loop continues after a ceiling hit. Both are right. 1.8 breaks only after a landing; a ceiling hit continues the loop on the new speed.

Correction: the reversed-gravity arms (1.01 '-6', 1.8 '-20', and the -20 that 1.18 and 1.24 describe as 'unchanged') are unreachable. With gravity reversed, both n2>0 and n2<0 enter the landing branch first. The 1.01 entry's 'or the floor under reversed gravity' should be dropped.

1.01 left-edge flip: with xPos == divisorLine the claim of a divisorLine-px error holds against the true world position. 1.8 itself is off by 156 there, because collisionDetection maps xPos == divisorLine to the right segment. Kept, with that caveat.

-1 px spawn: 'n2 - tileY*12 - 1' is in 1.9 (BounceCanvas.java:142), 1.12 (:145), 1.18 and 1.21 (d.java:146). Confirmed. 1.24 spawns at row*12+6 with no -1. Minor correction to 1.9: a ball under a ceiling first moves on the 4th update (ySpeed 0, 4, 8, 12), not on frame 3. With the minimum fall speed (1.18+) it moves on the 2nd.

Big-ball nudge removal: confirmed absent in 1.9 through 1.21. Its effect is corrected to 'none with the shipped levels'. The only candidate, the L11 checkpoint (143,45), is boxed in by deflators 39-42 (map dump). Deflators shrink on bounding-box contact, and tiles are tested column-major and top-down, so a 16-px ball always touches a deflator before or while it first overlaps the checkpoint. A big respawn there therefore looks unreachable, and the 1.18 report's 'deflator shrinks the ball before frame 1' should not occur in practice. This was reasoned from the code and the map, not run.

1.9 win path: displayGameOver no longer sets mState, and gameOver() is used only on death. Continue then calls displayGame(false); run() sees mLoadLevelFlag and createNewLevel keeps lives and score. Confirmed in CFR.

1.9 save: destroyApp calls saveGameData(3), which always writes -6 and uses an int[40][3] buffer. My level scan: L1-L10 have 15-35 save-relevant tiles at the start and L11 has exactly 50. So 1.9 can never save level 11, and the 50-entry array in 1.12+ just fits. Confirmed.

1.9 to 1.12 Ball CFR diff: only redirectBall and the ceiling line change (javap ineg/iconst_1/ishr). 1.12 has neither the minimum fall speed nor the brick flag change. Checked the 1.12 ramp examples by hand: tile 32 at (50,10) gives 1.8 (-5,-25) and 1.12 (50,-50). Confirmed.
End-of-game test: >= 11 in 1.01, 1.8, 1.9 and the port; > 11 in 1.12, 1.18, 1.21 and 1.24. Level files load as J2MElvl.%03d of mLevelNum, starting at 1. Confirmed.

Cheats: 1.12 has case 8 (FIRE) and still swallows -5. 1.18, 1.21 and 1.24 drop the -5 case and add case 35 ('#', antigravity counter = 300). Confirmed. Correction to the 1.21 report: invincibility is 7-8-7-8-9 then 8 (not 7-8-7-8-8), the same in every version.

1.12 to 1.18 normalised opcode diff (my ops.py) of update, testTile, thinCollide and collisionDetection: the only additions are the water bool with the minimum fall speed, and putfield w=true in the tile-1 hit branch (javap offsets 334-336). Confirmed.
Minimum fall speed disagreement: 1.18 has 's<10 && s>0 && !water'; 1.21 and 1.24 add '&& !antigravity'. Both reports are right. The 1.18 antigravity sinking follows from the code.

1.18 to 1.21 CFR diff, same obfuscation names: thinCollide size-1 and tile-1; bottom-rim edgeCollide size-1; spike box +1/-1; antigravity pickup sets grounded=false; the minimum fall speed guard; the screenFlip clamp fix (W-13, n2 += 156-(W-tileX)*12); level-complete Continue sets state 1; resetDirections in displayGame; save timestamp and DEADBEEF. So the 1.18 report's 'screenFlip identical to 1.8' is also right.

Edge-rim disagreement: 1.24's edgeCollide uses (x-g, y-g, x+g, y+g) for every case, the 1.8 size. 1.21's smaller bottom-rim box was reverted in 1.24. Both reports are right; the table lists it as not inherited.

1.24, all in CFR: pop l=7; enlarge from n=1; shrink only resizes; collisionDetection returns false at the first failing tile, and testTile keeps a local bl; spawn at tile*12+6 followed by enlarge for 16 px; flip test y-6 < R*12 or y+6 > R*12+96 with 7-row steps; camera clamp (W+1)*12-156 in scrolling and W*12-156 in recentre; exit test (al+1)*12 > camL && al*12 < camL+128 before the scroll call. That works out to opening when camL >= al*12-127, against about al*12-117 in 1.8, so 10 px earlier from the left and the same from the right. Level 1: W=112, exit col 110, so the camera stops at 1200 and only 8 px of the exit show. Confirmed.

Level 11 difference: cmp shows one byte, 1-based 7576 = 0-based 7575, 0x01 to 0x61, at row 42 col 91 (W=178). The two reports' offsets agree; one is 1-based. Level md5s: all other files are identical across all 8 builds, and .011 matches between 1.21 and 1.24.

Jump timing: my vertical-loop sim gives a held-jump cycle of 35 steps without the minimum fall speed and 33 with it, both with a 51-px apex. The apex hovers 5 steps against 2. This matches the 1.21 and 1.24 reports.

1.18 level-complete: the Continue command only calls setCurrent (state stays 5), and displayMainMenu shows Continue only if L==1 or a save exists. Confirmed. In 1.21 the same command sets M=1, so the bug is fixed there. Both builds, and 1.24, restart the timer under the form (stop, then a(false,0)). Confirmed.

132x176 port: r=132 in the left-end branches of createBufferFocused and screenFlip (e.java:114, :182). testScroll and scrollBuffer shift both edges, so the 132 width persists. Ball constants and the landing break match 1.8, and the HUD cap is 11. The mechanism is confirmed. The exact step numbers in the report (stop at step 76 vs 77, left stop at ball 67 vs 62) come from the reporter's own camera sim and were not re-run here.
